analysis.title: Global Thematics: Buy the Drop: AI Investment Opportunities Post the US Midterms
key_insights: Morgan Stanley calls the market reaction to the US midterms overdone and recommends a selective 'Buy the Drop' across AI enablers, infrastructure and adopters. The firm's AI capex projections are unchanged in aggregate, with a partial shift in data center builds from 2028 to 2029.

Newly elected governors are not expected to disrupt projects under construction, so 2027 is unchanged. Roughly 5GW of US projects not yet under construction in TX and OH move from 2028 to 2029, about 20% of US projects and 10% of global projects.

Post-shift, US data center GW additions fall 4% y/y in 2028 and rise 38% y/y in 2029. Globally, additions rise 9% in 2028 and 20% in 2029. US additions are 19.9GW in 2028 (was 24.9GW) and 27.6GW in 2029 (was 22.7GW).

Hyperscaler capex forecasts are unchanged at $1.6T in 2027 and $1.8T in 2028, with possible downward bias in 2028 if builds are delayed. Hyperscalers still earn ROIC above 30% on compute-intensive products.

The Powering AI model shows the 2028 US power shortfall widening to 44GW (38% of demanded power) from 38GW (33%). Morgan Stanley says the key bottleneck is shifting from compute to the powered shell stage.

A shift of the bottleneck to powered shell should erode pricing power in upstream compute components. Inventory build and slower orders are possible, and the supply chain could see a traditional down-cycle of margin normalization and earnings downgrades even with AI demand intact. Memory and Intel are flagged as most exposed in semis.

Morgan Stanley's three buckets are hyperscalers (AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT, SPCX plus NVDA as the key semi), de-rated data center supply chain names (powered shell, behind-the-meter power, IPPs, energy, APAC developers, compute semis, HDD and optical), and software enablers and AI adopters as alpha broadens.

Compute is the highest-conviction semis bucket (NVDA, AVGO, TSMC, MediaTek, Samsung). NVDA is the top pick, on a larger customer base, revenue per GW rising from about $40bn with Rubin to above $50bn with Feynman, and tokens per watt leadership. NVDA and AVGO trade near 9x CY28 P/E.

Memory is a tactical buy despite pricing risk. Multiples have compressed and buybacks are accretive. Sandisk at $835 with buybacks near 50% of revenue could repurchase more than 50% of the company by end-2028. Analog is seen as less attractive risk/reward and networking multiples are not yet as attractive.

Semis strategy: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down about 40% since mid-June. Strategists think the correction is nearing its end and price action resolves upward into 2027, though a final retest cannot be ruled out on positioning and technicals. The S&P 500 nears the 7100-7300 support range.

Data center capex is 5% of 2027 consensus S&P 500 revenue and mid-single digits in 2028. Even if capacity is pushed out, the impact on S&P revenue and earnings is seen as limited and priced in at 18x forward earnings, near Liberation Day valuation levels.

Texas: Governor-elect Hinojosa's platform pauses new data center approvals but allows approved and under-construction projects to finish. The legislature is split (Democratic House, Republican Senate), which limits durable changes. Ohio's governor-elect proposed a conditional moratorium on new permits and Republicans keep both chambers. Georgia is incremental.

Powered shell providers: WULF, RIOT, HUT and APLD are less exposed to Texas dynamics. CIFR, GLXY and MARA face greater risk of delay or moratorium. Morgan Stanley assigns 75% probability that CIFR's Colchis and GLXY's Helios II and Merlin I receive required approvals, and about 10% for studied-load projects ultimately getting interconnection.

Power equipment and IPPs: BE, SEI, VST, TLN and CEG are high-conviction Overweights even if data center growth is slower. GEV and INIO are valuation-supported but more sensitive to oversupply. Backlog risk is limited for GEV, BE, INIO and SEI due to deposits and cancellation provisions. PJM exposure (TLN, CEG) is preferred over ERCOT.

Utilities: Morgan Stanley is cautiously constructive on TX utilities with SRE and AEP Overweight, negative on SO (governor weighing a moratorium and a Democratic majority on the PSC). It expects a shift toward defensive utilities AEE, ED, DUK, PPL and to stay in ETR for Louisiana exposure.

Multi-industry and machinery: the risk skews to new entrants (ACCV, FPS, CARR) rather than legacy leaders (VRT, ETN, TT, JCI). CAT, CMI and EROC are most exposed to de-rating, with CAT more than the others. Rental companies (URI, WSC, TH) are oversold and the analyst would be buyers. Aggregates are neutral to positive.

Credit: AI-related debt supply is about $543bn year to date versus $216bn in FY25. Hyperscalers are about 60% of supply and 2027 issuance is expected to exceed 2026. New construction financing and neoclouds face more scrutiny. Stabilized assets benefit and colocation ABS is preferred over hyperscaler data center ABS.

Oracle: three roughly 1GW campuses (Jupiter NM, Lighthouse WI, Shackelford TX) sit in states with incoming governors who signaled restrictions. They are tied to more than $50bn of short-dated construction loans. Morgan Stanley keeps a cautious credit stance on ORCL and does not yet recommend stepping in.

Asia: spillover of US data center demand could reach about 15GW in Asia and 20GW globally from other markets. Winners named are Gulf Development, Keppel, Adani Power, Yangtze Power, Samsung SDI and Hokkaido Electric. KEPCO, Tata Power, Global Power Synergy, Huaneng and Electric Power Development are to avoid. Asia cloud semis suppliers Aspeed and Montage face risk over the next 2-4 quarters.

ASML: the market is pricing about 93 EUV Low NA tools in FY28, roughly flat y/y and 16% below consensus. ASML trades at 16.6x FY28 consensus EPS. Overweight, Top Pick, PT 1,700 euros on a 25x multiple of FY28 EPS of 68.47 euros.

China: lower data center and power constraints. Morgan Stanley prefers the self-sufficiency AI trade (CXMT, Cambricon) and expects slower US capex or tighter US AI regulation to favor Chinese open-weight models. Alibaba, Tencent, Z.ai and MiniMax are named beneficiaries.

Rotation to adopters: 44% of S&P 500 companies cite a quantifiable AI benefit, up from 32%. Financials are furthest along. Companies that frequently quantify benefits show faster NTM EPS growth. Europe's AI enablers have given back nearly 50% of relative performance versus AI-challenged stocks, which Morgan Stanley calls overdone.
LatAm: more tied to AI infrastructure through copper and lithium. Chile and Mexico are most impacted, with Mexico's IT hardware exports to the US up 101% y/y in 9M26. Axia is the preferred exposure.

Catalysts: possible Texas special session, PUCT confirmation, bills filed in Texas next week, the December 10 finalization of the Texas data center audit and ERCOT certification meetings on December 10 and 17, incoming governors' plans in January, and FERC PJM decisions in early 2027.

earnings_insights: MSFT guided to 49-50% cc Azure growth in fiscal 2Q (company guidance) with some third-party GPU capacity shifting into 2HFY27, per Morgan Stanley.

ORCL delivered about 850MW in its most recent quarter (1FQ27, company-reported) and expects about 6GW more by FY28 for a total of 10GW. Guidance embeds cushion for up to a couple of quarters of delay at four sites.
INIO reported 19GW of contracts at end of 3Q26 (company-reported), of which Morgan Stanley estimates about 12GW are firm orders.
GEV had 122GW of gas under contract at FY3Q26 (company-reported).
CoreWeave management said moratoriums will affect where infrastructure is built, not the demand for it. Phase I of its Helios site (133MW) was delivered in July.

ASML reported record order intake in 1H26 per Morgan Stanley and trades at 16.6x FY28 consensus EPS. MS models 94 EUV shipments in FY27 and 111 in FY28, while management points to capacity for 90 tools in FY27 and more than 110 in FY28.
Hyperscaler 3Q26 results confirmed AI growth, but stocks did not react positively, per the Asia semis team.
RIOT's Corsicana lease generates a 33% yield on cost (discussed in MS 3Q26 earnings note), with rent beginning in September 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Buy hyperscalers AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT and SPCX on the post-midterm drop
trade_ideas.rationale: Scale, capital access and LLM efficiency gains position the largest players to gain share and margin.
trade_ideas.risk: Delays in project approvals could bias 2028 capex lower and a higher data center tax structure would raise build costs.

trade_ideas.description: Buy NVDA as top pick in semis
trade_ideas.rationale: Larger customer base, revenue per GW rising to above $50bn with Feynman, and tokens-per-watt leadership.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower GW build could cause inventory builds and lower pricing power for in-shortage components.

trade_ideas.description: Buy de-rated power and IPP names BE, SEI, VST, TLN and CEG
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuation support and contract protections hold even if data center growth is slower.
trade_ideas.risk: A prolonged slowdown beyond 2028 would loosen supply chains for engines and fuel cells.

trade_ideas.description: Buy ASML as Top Pick for outperformance amid weaker AI sentiment
trade_ideas.rationale: Market implies flat FY28 EUV shipments while no slowing is seen in DRAM or logic.
trade_ideas.risk: Capacity concerns and China competition or export restrictions.

trade_ideas.description: Buy de-rated memory MU and SNDK tactically
trade_ideas.rationale: Multiple compression and accretive buybacks offset the softer pricing risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower GW deployment could soften memory pricing.

trade_ideas.description: Buy HDD names STX and WDC and optical networking names LITE, COHR, ANET and KEYS that de-rated
trade_ideas.rationale: De-rated areas of tech hardware with attractive risk/reward.
trade_ideas.risk: Customers could hold excess inventory in a slowdown.

trade_ideas.description: Buy equipment rental companies URI, WSC and TH
trade_ideas.rationale: Project backlogs are further along in permitting and construction, and the group is oversold.
trade_ideas.risk: URI has mega-project exposure in a bear case for data centers.

trade_ideas.description: Buy ORCL 5Y CDS, entered at +57bp on 9/28/25, now +313bp (Morgan Stanley credit trade)
trade_ideas.rationale: Credit profile deterioration from cash funding needs and rising lease liabilities for new data centers.
trade_ideas.risk: Constructive RPO and financing updates, creative financing support, and CDS technicals such as basis selling.

trade_ideas.description: Sell ORCL 5.2% 9/26/35 bond, entered at +167bp on 1/23/26, now +309bp (Morgan Stanley credit trade)
trade_ideas.rationale: Credit profile deterioration driven by funding needs and lease liabilities.
trade_ideas.risk: Creative financing support and additional visibility on long-term monetization and delevering beyond FY28.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer colocation data center ABS over hyperscaler data center ABS shelves
trade_ideas.rationale: Colocation shelves have wider geographic diversification and benefit from scarcity of operating capacity.

risk_factors: More challenging than expected labor requirements, bans on on-site fossil generation (as in Virginia), or tighter emissions limits could lower data center deployments versus projections.
A prolonged slowdown beyond 2028 would loosen supply chains for engines and fuel cells and hurt demand for large gas turbines.
An air-pocket in 2028 across the tech supply chain could reduce pricing power or build inventory, with margin sustainability the key risk.
Financing headwinds and investor angst could matter more than slower construction. New construction financings and neoclouds face greater scrutiny.
Possible special session in Texas, PUCT appointments and the legislature's treatment of 765kV transmission could change the regulatory balance.
Utilities risk lower allowed financial parameters as governors push affordability.
Single-site headlines, such as the Jupiter force majeure, can weigh on broader sentiment.
Mexico's IT hardware exports to the US are tied to US data center construction, and a slowdown would hit assembly and industrial real estate.
vol_and_positioning: Morgan Stanley's composite sentiment and positioning indicator is nearing capitulatory levels but is not quite at the March selloff levels.
A final retest is possible on leveraged ETF and macro systematic supply dynamics and a final spike in correlation.
Median semis stock is down 53% from its 52-week high and the average is down 48%.
Geothermal and AI power stocks have de-grossed, with FRVO down 40% over the last month.
DLR and EQIX shares show higher beta to AI-related headline volatility.
geopolitical: US midterm results: Democrats won the House and Senate, and governorships in Ohio, Texas and Georgia, raising state-level data center pushback.
Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa proposes pausing new data center approvals, and Ohio's governor-elect proposes a conditional moratorium.
Texas Governor Abbott ordered an audit of data center projects in the ERCOT queue in August. Interconnection requests reached about 474GW.
No federal pause is expected given the national-security framing and likely presidential veto, according to Morgan Stanley's strategists.
US-China competition continues. A Democratic Congress may reduce abrupt trade actions but bipartisan tech and security concerns persist.
Possible Iran de-escalation is cited as a potential pressure on midstream stocks.
Recent regional conflict may have reduced the near-term attractiveness of the Middle East as a host for US data center capacity.

tension_points.bull_case: A shift of about 5GW from 2028 to 2029 elongates the capex cycle, smooths supply-demand rebalancing, improves credit and raises lease rates for compute, with hyperscalers best positioned.
tension_points.bear_case: A 2028 air-pocket could reduce supply chain pricing power, build inventory and trigger margin normalization and earnings downgrades, and tougher rules could turn a delay into a reduction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Labor requirements tougher than expected, bans on on-site fossil generation, or stricter emissions limits that cut deployments, and a prolonged slowdown in construction beyond 2028.

tension_points.bull_case: Multiple compression and large buybacks make memory a tactical buy, with DRAM and NAND tight as at any point in the cycle.
tension_points.bear_case: A slower GW build could let supply catch up to demand, causing inventory builds and softer pricing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Clear signs of pricing erosion or order cancellations in memory.

tension_points.bull_case: Current assets and contracts support valuations well above current prices, and companies are hedged through 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: A Texas moratorium would reduce data center upside and loosen ERCOT supply and demand.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Texas legislative action beyond permit pauses, such as ending the sales-tax exemption or giving localities power to reject projects.
